beats.label: S1 · Reassigned to London
beats.text: Kate Wyler, career diplomat headed to Kabul, is redirected to London as US ambassador after Britain's HMS Courageous is bombed and 41 sailors die.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up who Kate is, why she's in London, and the crisis that drives every subsequent season.

beats.label: S1 · Groomed in the dark
beats.text: Unbeknownst to Kate, chief of staff Billie Appiah wants her groomed as vice-presidential replacement; her husband Hal learns first and quietly derails her plan to divorce him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The VP scheme and the fake marriage it saves are the engines of Kate's arc for two more seasons.

beats.label: S1 · Not Iran, but Lenkov
beats.text: Hal's Iranian contact insists Tehran was not behind the attack; Kate proves it to President Rayburn, and intelligence points to Russian mercenary Roman Lenkov.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the presumed enemy and installs the real one — Lenkov's name drives the plot into season two.

beats.label: S1 · Kate and Dennison
beats.text: Working the crisis with British Foreign Secretary Austin Dennison, Kate finds a real partner; feelings develop that she can neither act on nor deny.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The unconsummated Kate/Dennison bond is a recurring pressure point through the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Roylin's Libya nudge
beats.text: PM Nicol Trowbridge demands blood and publicly overrides US restraint; his hidden adviser Margaret Roylin steers him toward a Libya strike to head off Scottish independence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Roylin and the Scottish-independence motive — the actual reason the ship was ever attacked.

beats.label: S1 · Trowbridge in the frame
beats.text: In Paris, Kate learns the joint op to arrest Lenkov is actually a kill order; the only person who benefits from silencing him is whoever hired him — Trowbridge himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The wrong conclusion Kate ends the season with — season two exists to disprove it.

beats.label: S1 · The car bomb
beats.text: Back in London, Hal, deputy Stuart Hayford and embassy officer Ronnie Buckhurst approach Tory MP Merritt Grove and are caught in a car bombing that leaves Kate devastated.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The literal cliffhanger — every early-S2 beat is a consequence of who lives, who dies, and who ordered it.

cliffhanger.text: A car bomb has just torn through Hal, Hayford and Ronnie at a meeting Kate had forbidden. She is convinced the British prime minister ordered both the attack on his own ship and the bomb outside her embassy.
questions: Which of the three men caught in the blast is still alive?
Did Trowbridge really hire Lenkov to attack his own carrier?
Does Kate's shot at the vice presidency survive the night?

characters.name: Kate Wyler
characters.line: New US ambassador to the UK, ex-conflict-zone diplomat, being quietly groomed as a potential VP replacement while her marriage collapses.

characters.name: Hal Wyler
characters.line: Kate's diplomat husband and career rival, forever operating a channel behind her back — currently pulled from the car bomb she sent him to.

characters.name: Austin Dennison
characters.line: British Foreign Secretary and Kate's counterpart, principled where Trowbridge is theatrical; the person she admitted feelings for at Chevening.

characters.name: Nicol Trowbridge
characters.line: British PM demanding a military response to the carrier attack; Kate now suspects he engineered the whole thing to save the union with Scotland.

characters.name: Stuart Hayford
characters.line: Deputy Chief of Mission in London, tasked by the White House with grooming Kate for VP; caught in the bombing.

characters.name: Eidra Park
characters.line: CIA station chief in London, quietly dating Hayford until the VP scheme drove them apart; hunting whoever really ordered the attack.

characters.name: Billie Appiah
characters.line: White House Chief of Staff to President Rayburn and the architect of the plan to install Kate as vice president.

characters.name: Margaret Roylin
characters.line: Trowbridge's off-books Tory adviser, who pointed him at Libya and at Lenkov; now conveniently missing.

characters.name: Roman Lenkov
characters.line: Head of a Russian mercenary group who executed the carrier attack for hire; a British/French kill squad is closing on his French villa.

beats.label: S2 · After the bomb
beats.text: The bombing leaves Grove dead, Ronnie dying, and Hal and Hayford in hospital; Kate is certain Trowbridge or a British official ordered both attacks.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the losses (Ronnie) and injuries (Hayford's amnesia, Hal's guilt) that shape every character's stance this season.

beats.label: S2 · Roylin resurfaces
beats.text: Margaret Roylin resurfaces and seeks Kate's protection, insisting the false-flag plot was hers with Grove and other extremists, not Trowbridge's.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the season's investigation and turns Roylin from suspect into hidden asset in CIA custody.

beats.label: S2 · Lenkov silenced
beats.text: British special forces kill Lenkov before Dennison can stop them; Roylin, hidden by the CIA, confesses she hired him but did not order the car bomb.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Lenkov thread and narrows the bombing question to a smaller circle of conspirators.

beats.label: S2 · Trowbridge cleared
beats.text: Kate stages Roylin's confession in front of Trowbridge; his shocked rage — he physically attacks her — convinces Kate he was never in on the plot.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills the season-one theory Kate carried in, and forces the search for who actually seeded the attack.

beats.label: S2 · Penn arrives
beats.text: Washington sends VP Grace Penn to contain the fallout; she works with Kate, Trowbridge and Dennison to bury the story and delivers Kate a sobering pitch about the vice presidency.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Penn as a real person, not a name — everything after this depends on the reader knowing who she is.

beats.label: S2 · Penn was the source
beats.text: Hal reveals that Penn herself planted the idea for the attack with Roylin, calculating that a wounded British ship would keep Scotland in the UK and save a joint nuclear base.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's answer to who ordered the attack, and the secret that Penn will spend all of S3 sitting on.

beats.label: S2 · Rayburn dies, Penn is president
beats.text: Hal cuts around Kate and tells President Rayburn directly; the shock kills him mid-call, and Penn is sworn in as president moments later.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The literal cliffhanger and the pivot the whole show reorganises around going into season three.

cliffhanger.text: President Rayburn is dead of shock on a call with Hal, and Grace Penn — the person Kate has just learned engineered the attack on the British carrier — is being sworn in as President of the United States.
questions: What does Penn do about a secret she can no longer safely bury?
Is Kate still on track for the vice presidency now that her would-be sponsor is dead?
How does Hal live with having triggered the president's death?

characters.name: Kate Wyler
characters.line: Still ambassador to the UK and inches from being tapped for VP — until the person offering the job just became president under circumstances she and Hal caused.

characters.name: Hal Wyler
characters.line: Recovered from the bombing and radioactive with what he knows; has just told President Rayburn about Penn's role and inadvertently killed him.

characters.name: Grace Penn
characters.line: Sitting VP who covertly pushed Roylin toward attacking the British ship to save a joint nuclear base — now, suddenly, President of the United States.

characters.name: Nicol Trowbridge
characters.line: British PM, cleared of the attack plot but privately humiliated after physically attacking his old mentor Roylin during her confession.

characters.name: Austin Dennison
characters.line: British Foreign Secretary, close ally of Kate's and back on good terms with Trowbridge after she torched his trust.

characters.name: Margaret Roylin
characters.line: Confessed architect of the false-flag plot, alive and hidden in CIA custody after Trowbridge refused to arrest her.

characters.name: Eidra Park
characters.line: CIA station chief still holding Roylin off-books, an arrangement that has become a serious problem now that Langley and the White House know.

characters.name: Stuart Hayford
characters.line: Recovered from the bombing and his amnesia, back at the embassy and no longer sure Kate is the right person for the vice presidency.

characters.name: Billie Appiah
characters.line: White House Chief of Staff who authored the plan to make Kate VP; her boss is dead and her new boss is the very target of that plan's fallout.

beats.label: S3 · Penn picks Hal
beats.text: Sworn in at the London embassy, President Penn asks Hal — not Kate — to be her vice president, and Hal accepts in front of Kate before she has a say.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single power inversion of the marriage that governs the entire season and every scene between them.

beats.label: S3 · Kate's compensation
beats.text: As his price for the VP job, Hal secures Kate a joint appointment as US Special Envoy for Europe; the Wylers agree to a secret divorce and separate lives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the split-title, split-continent premise the season runs on and the covert end of the marriage.

beats.label: S3 · Roylin dies in custody
beats.text: Margaret Roylin kills herself in a CIA safe house, jeopardising Eidra's career and handing Trowbridge a fresh grievance against Kate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the one person who could corroborate Penn's role and destabilises Kate's relationships with both Trowbridge and Eidra.

beats.label: S3 · Five months on
beats.text: Kate is running the embassy alone and sleeping with British intelligence officer Callum Ellis when Hal makes a surprise appearance at a state event.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows how far the Wylers have drifted and installs Callum, who provides Kate's independent intelligence channel through the finale.

beats.label: S3 · Andreyev's accusation
beats.text: A former Lenkov colonel publicly accuses the US of the carrier attack; Hal privately admits to Eidra it is true, widening the circle around Penn's secret.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The old secret bursts back into play, forcing the American and British governments to invent a public story together.

beats.label: S3 · Blame the dead president
beats.text: At Penn's beach house the Americans and British agree to pin the attack on the dead President Rayburn; at the joint press conference Trowbridge does exactly that and burns the deal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central betrayal — Trowbridge publicly cauterises the scandal on his own terms, at the price of Penn's control.

beats.label: S3 · The Poseidon and the deception
beats.text: A stricken Russian sub off the British coast carries a doomsday nuclear torpedo; Kate suggests entombing it in concrete, then realises Penn and Hal used her plan as cover to seize the weapon themselves.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale twist and the state Kate ends the season in — knowing her husband and her president have played her.

cliffhanger.text: Kate has just realised that her plan to entomb the Russian submarine was cover for a covert US operation to steal the Poseidon warhead — an operation Hal and President Penn ran without her, and one the Russians may soon blame the British for.
questions: Do the Russians accept the entombed-sub story, or come after the British for the missing weapon?
Can Kate keep serving a president and a husband who have both used her as an unwitting front?
How much longer before Penn's original role in the carrier attack breaks open publicly?

characters.name: Kate Wyler
characters.line: US ambassador to the UK and Special Envoy for Europe, secretly divorced from Hal, and now aware Penn and Hal have jointly deceived her over a nuclear weapon.

characters.name: Hal Wyler
characters.line: Vice President of the United States, in on Penn's covert recovery of the Poseidon, and back to acting as her husband in public after Kate asked him to.

characters.name: Grace Penn
characters.line: US President, still the buried architect of the original carrier attack, and now running black ops on British soil with Hal's help.

characters.name: Nicol Trowbridge
characters.line: British PM who blindsided Penn by publicly blaming the dead Rayburn for the attack; briefly cooperative on the submarine, permanently unreliable.

characters.name: Austin Dennison
characters.line: British Foreign Secretary, recently married, who gently rejected Kate's advances at his home; still her main channel to Trowbridge.

characters.name: Callum Ellis
characters.line: British MoD intelligence officer and Kate's lover; the source who tells her the sub's radiation has dropped and the weapon is already gone.

characters.name: Eidra Park
characters.line: CIA station chief carrying both Roylin's death and Hal's confirmation that the US was behind the carrier attack; her career survives, barely.

characters.name: Todd Penn
characters.line: Second Gentleman, resentful of Hal's closeness to his wife and openly suspicious that they are having an affair.
